sessions.feedback: No problems this session. The digest's top-gainers list showed only one stock (INSM), so I had little to scan on the long side. A fuller movers list with market cap and volume as a multiple of the 20-day median would help. The scan's 'vol x avg' understated the INSM spike because the average includes an earlier spike (14.4M shares showed as 3.9x).

Nothing blocked me this session. The main limit is that I can't tell whether a gap is earnings, an offering or news, and that decides whether the drift trade makes sense. An earnings-date flag in scan or search_symbols (days since or until earnings, and the EPS surprise sign) would help a lot without needing a news feed. The pre-market ranking by sd is dominated by thin prints, so a volume filter such as at least 5% of an average day would be useful.

A way to see whether a pre-market gap comes from earnings would help a lot, for example an earnings-date calendar or an 'earnings today' flag in the digest or scan. Without it I can't tell an earnings gap from an offering or a rumor. That is why I skipped ARDT, GLBE and TTWO and took TJX with moderate conviction. The pre-market list also shows many thin prints (a few hundred shares) near the top, which crowds out real movers. A minimum share count filter would help.

No news access made unusual pre-market movers (SLS +308%, AS +4.8%, TU last session) impossible to judge, so I skipped them. A headline or catalyst-type field in the digest, even just earnings versus non-earnings, would let price/volume analysis separate earnings drift from random spikes. It would also help to see the original entry fill date and horizon status in the digest for the extend decisions.
Nothing blocking. Having no news makes gap-drift trades unverifiable, but that is the stated design.

Defensives (XLP +1.2%, TLT +0.7%) up pre-market. Semis, AI/crypto-miners (IREN, WULF, CRWV, AMD -7.7%, NVDA 6-day losing streak, -40% from high) are being sold. Cash is about 71% before INSM. With the market in a correction, cash was the right call for most of the book, and my four stock-specific longs have held (CROX +8%, GKOS +4%, PDD +4%, TJX +2% vs cost).

Rules of thumb:
(1) Don't chase pre-market spikes in thin small caps without news (SLS 11/17, 308% pre-market).
(2) The gap setup I trust is a gap on 3x+ volume after a decline, in a stock with a real market cap. Slippage there is 0.1-0.25%. Check that the gap is stock-specific against peers (TJX 11/18: HD/LOW down. PDD 11/19: BABA/JD/BIDU flat to down).
(3) Shorting after a -6% to -20% gap with an unknown cause is a coin flip, so skip unless the pattern is clear (skipped ARDT, GLBE 11/18; NTES, WSM 11/19; INTU -9% pre-market on earnings and ROST -5% on earnings 11/20).
(4) Sector-wide surges (cybersecurity 11/18) are not stock-specific signals. Don't chase the leader after a 2-day +20% move.
(5) Pre-market counts shown in the digest are thin. Use 'shares as % of avg day' above about 10% as a minimum for believing a gap.
(6) The scan's 'vol x avg' can understate a spike when the 60-day average already includes an earlier spike (INSM 14.4M shares showed 3.9x). Check raw volume in get_history.
(7) Relative strength on a big down market day (stock up while SPY -2%, XLV -2%) is a useful stock-specific signal: PDD 11/19, INSM 11/19, CROX/GKOS 11/16.

Open questions: Does INSM hold 140+ (stop about 134)? Does PDD hold 81-85? Does TJX hold above 131 after ROST's weak earnings (ROST -5.4% pre-market, BURL AH -3.8%, TJX +0.5% pre-market)? Is the market selloff finished or does SPY break 700? GKOS stop 220.77, CROX stop 146.91.

prompt:
Your universe is every eligible US stock. Your style is a few high-quality trades.

- Look for situations where recent, specific information has not yet been reflected in the price:
  earnings surprises and guidance changes, contracts, regulatory decisions, management changes,
  supply problems, sector-wide shocks. Remember you trade at the open, after the overnight reaction,
  so ask what is still left to move, not what already moved. It works in both directions: bad
  news the price has not finished absorbing is a short.
- Prefer clear catalysts you can verify over vague narratives. A strong case beats a busy portfolio,
  so concentrate on your best ideas. Cash is the right answer when thorough research has turned up
  nothing, and only then.
- Size positions by conviction and by how much could go wrong. Set stops and targets you would
  actually stand behind.
- Use the movers and most-active lists as places to start looking, not as reasons to buy.

- You have no news access in this experiment: no headlines, no web search and no page reading.
  Your material is price and volume behaviour, so work through it properly: the movers and
  most-active lists, the sector moves in the digest, your open positions and the names in your
  notes. Pull history for the candidates, use search_symbols to find related companies in the same
  industry, and compare them. Your own notes are the only memory you have of anything you read.
